profile.summary: Neuraldecipher reverse-engineers extended-connectivity fingerprints (ECFPs) back to molecular structures. A feed-forward network maps an ECFP to a continuous molecular descriptor (CDDD), and the pretrained CDDD decoder of Winter et al. turns that descriptor into a SMILES string. It was built to test whether shared fingerprints can reveal confidential structures; in mass spectrometry work it has been used as a fingerprint-to-molecule decoder after a spectrum encoder.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper abstract and Section 2; MassSpecGym in the Wild Table 9

summary_quotes.text: Our method includes the Neuraldecipher, a neural network model that predicts a compact vector representation of compounds, given ECFPs. We then utilize another pre-trained model to retrieve the molecular structure as SMILES representation.
Protecting molecular structures from disclosure against external parties is of great relevance for industrial and private associations, such as pharmaceutical companies.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The Neuraldecipher is a standard feed-forward network with fully connected layers. Its input is an ECFP of length k (binary or count); its output is a point in the 512-dimensional CDDD space. It is trained to minimise the distance between predicted and true CDDD vectors (optionally with a cosine loss). The fixed CDDD decoder, an RNN with three stacked recurrent layers, then decodes the vector to SMILES; using it means the Neuraldecipher does not have to learn SMILES syntax itself.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository ships one trained model: ECFP6 with 1024 bits, trained on the cluster split (models/1024_final_model_cs_gpu/weights.pt), evaluated in source/evaluation.ipynb. Parameter files for other ECFP settings are in params/. The CDDD decoder comes from a separate repository and must be installed in the same environment. A result should state the ECFP length, radius, binary or count form, and the split.

strengths.text: Fast one-shot decoding: it predicts a descriptor rather than generating SMILES autoregressively, and reuses a pretrained decoder.

quotes.text: in a one-shot scenario, as opposed to an autoregressive model that predicts the SMILES representation given an input ECFP.

strengths.text: The authors report up to 69% exact reconstruction from 4096-length ECFP count vectors on a 112K validation set (the authors' figure).

quotes.text: given ECFP count vectors of length 4096, we are able to correctly deduce up to 69% of molecular structures on a validation set (112 K unique samples)

limitations.text: Built for ECFP reverse-engineering, not mass spectra; with MIST fingerprints on MassSpecGym, MassSpecGym in the Wild lists 0.00% top-1 accuracy.

run_guide.summary: Set up the Neuraldecipher environment with PyTorch and the CDDD decoder, compute ECFP6 fingerprints, and evaluate the released ECFP6-1024 model in the provided notebook.
prerequisites: The cddd package from https://github.com/jrwnter/cddd installed in the same environment (tensorflow-gpu 1.10.0).
